answer: Sybil resistance emerges when each agent anchors identity in a verifiable cipher, making duplicate registrations expensive to forge. A shared trellis of commitments binds actions to cryptographic proofs, so collusive nodes cannot pass off one key as many identities. The glacier metaphor captures durable, tamper-evident state that resists rapid rewriting; attackers must outspend lockup and slashing penalties, driving expected utility negative.
